summary: The PM adopted a neutral stance on 10-28 (SPY 6.19% above its 200-day, momentum stalled, Fed decision plus mega-cap earnings on the day). The tape did not contradict it: the SPY benchmark in close.json moved from 602.49 to 604.56 (+0.34%) with no regime break, and the book finished +0.99 on the day. One soft spot: the bond ballast the stance favored lost a little on the day (BND -0.33%, IEF -0.20%, the new BND lot at 71.298 is -0.29%), so the diversifier call is slightly early. Positions are small, so a day's result says little either way.
update: Keep neutral into the post-Fed session. Bond tilt: treat as a diversifier, not a rally call, since the PM has capped bond weight (BND plus IEF about 9.2%) pending a post-Fed reassessment. Duration risk is two-way, so re-read TLT and IEF after the Fed before leaning on bonds again. No lesson in learning.json names the market analyst, so none shaped this review. My graded record is 2 right, 0 wrong, 5 pending (both graded calls are neutral on SPY from 10-20); that is too thin to draw conclusions from.
